messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Elevated 5xx + connection resets observed for /v1/stream in us-east-1 and us-west-2. Error-rate ~20% over 10m. Paging oncall.

Maya Rivera: I'm on. Seeing alerts in the dashboards. Which stack component reports the 5xx?

Owen Park: Frontend gateway (envoy) returning 502/504 to customers. Traces show 'upstream reset' and 'connection refused' from runtime backends. Logs show a lot of partial chunk writes followed by connection closed.

Priya Singh: Runtime (model-serving) reports: 
```
2026-03-14T12:34:12.998Z WARN stream_sink: write chunk failed: broken pipe (EPIPE)
2026-03-14T12:34:13.004Z INFO stream_handler: client_cancelled id=0x9a2f reason="socket closed by client"
```

Liam O'Connor: SDK telemetry indicates several clients (some large customers) are using aggressive reconnect logic on stream disconnects; they retry immediately which creates a tight retry loop.

Maya Rivera: Two-prong mitigation: 1) reduce retry storm by adding short circuit on gateway per-UID reconnect rate limiting, 2) make streaming route tolerant by switching to proxy-buffered response (envoy buffer) for a short window so clients see final payloads instead of chunk transitions. Thoughts?

Owen Park: Proxy buffering introduces latency spikes for large generation but should stop chunk-parsing resets. Alternatively, we can route streaming traffic to the dedicated streaming fleet (dedicated-pool-a) which has a higher connection limit and different kernel tuning. Routing change is heavier.

Priya Singh: A quick config we can flip: in envoy route add `proxy_buffer_body=true` for /v1/stream and a header rewrite `Connection: close` for clients that look flaky. I'll prepare the config and push to canary.

deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout (cfg-1860012) to envoy-canary-2 group.

Nora Patel: I'll open an emergency support notice to affected customers and include the workaround (client-side: exponential backoff, implement jitter). Draft: "We are investigating intermittent streaming failures; we have applied a temporary routing change to improve delivery and reduce retries. Please update SDKs to 2.3.2+ when available."

Maya Rivera: Can someone check kernel stats on the runtime nodes? Maybe we have many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT or a FD leak causing resets.

Priya Singh: Checking now. Some runtime hosts show higher than normal 'time_wait' and a spike in open fds around the same time window. Suspect abrupt client disconnects leaving half-open connections.

Owen Park: Canary metrics: after proxy-buffer enabling on canary group, 5xx dropped from 19% to 2% within 90s. Tail latency on canary increased by ~120ms median for those requests.

deploy-bot: Rolling to 30% of gateways. Estimated finish 45s.

incident-bot: Tagging incident: "streaming-connectivity"; added severity P1. Handoff to SRE for follow-up.

Maya Rivera: Given customer impact, we're going to expand to 100% for now — acceptable tradeoff: slightly higher latency for stabilized success rates. Proceeding to full roll.

deploy-bot: Rolling update to 100% (cfg-1860012). Rollout complete.

Liam O'Connor: After rollout, observed client behavior: many clients immediately reconnected and eventually gave up, some clients retried in parallel leading to bursts. We've added a short server-side cookie `x-rw-retry-suggest: 2000` instructing SDKs to delay 2s before reconnect; SDK team will honor this header in next release.

Priya Singh: Runtime teams are also increasing keepalive probes and adjusting socket linger to ensure server closes cleanly. Planning kernel tuning ticket: reduce tcp_fin_timeout and ensure ephemeral port reuse is healthy.

Nora Patel: Customer impact estimate: approx 32% of long-running streaming sessions (>20s) in affected regions saw at least one failure during window. Affected customers reported degraded UX; no data loss reported.

Maya Rivera: Post-mitigation actions:
- short: keep proxy-buffering for streaming route for 24h while we harden parsing and backpressure
- medium: patch runtime to tolerate mid-stream cancels and avoid EPIPE crashes
- medium: add per-client reconnect throttles at the gateway + SDK backoff improvements
- long: migration plan to dedicated streaming fleet with tuned kernel and larger conn limits

Owen Park: I've captured traces and pcap snippets to s3://redwood-incidents/1860012345/trace-pcaps.tgz and created ticket RINF-1872 for the kernel/socket investigation.

deploy-bot: Configuration cfg-1860012 applied and persisted.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to P2.

Maya Rivera: Handing to oncall for post-incident clean up and PM for customer comms. Owen will drive the triage.

Owen Park: I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with SDK and runtime teams. Linking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RINF-1872. Will include timeline, root-cause hypothesis, and tests.

Nora Patel: Posting final customer message draft to #customer-notifications for review.

Maya Rivera: Good work everyone. Keep related artifacts in the ticket. Closing immediate thread. :white_check_mark:
